newsitem.title: USA: Rising water in Louisiana brings unwelcome guests.
newsitem.headline: Rising water in Louisiana brings unwelcome guests.

text.p: Rising water from the Mississippi River is bringing more than just the threat of flooding to south Louisiana -- unwelcome visitors are now slithering into residential neighborhoods.

Venomous and non-poisonous snakes and alligators have been turning up in populated areas bordering the river and smaller tributaries that have overflowed their banks because the river is too full to drain them, authorities said.
The river, swollen by floodwaters from the Ohio and upper Mississippi valleys, is expected to crest next week at its highest level since 1927. There is no immediate danger to populated areas.
But the reptiles, displaced by the backwater flooding and a spillway opening to relieve pressure on levees near New Orleans, have spread out and been washed into new territory.
Authorities in New Orleans and its suburbs have issued advisories to weekend joggers, bikers, rollerbladers and picknickers near Lake Pontchartrain and river levee recreation areas.
An Orleans Levee District Police spokesman said the problem occured any time there was a threat of major flooding. "You just have to watch where you step and what you pick up," he said.
